limitations: Synthetic local subprocess behavior is not provider schema compatibility or semantic model qualification.
Process launch, I/O and OS scheduling are not hard real-time; trusted workers are required, not a hostile-code sandbox.
POSIX descendants that leave the process group are outside containment; root reaping is observed, not all descendants.
Source freeze and Python version are not a hermetic environment, CLI binary identity or authenticated remote model.
Worker invocations do not count hidden provider requests. No new real-call budget, migration of approvals, default promotion or sprint completion.
summary: Opt-in source-frozen transport supervises one fixed JSON worker per charged stage, with monotonic call/session budgets, cleanup reserve, Windows Job Object/POSIX session, durable attempts/receipts and offline replay. New authorization covers exact outer policy and nested flow.
